kicker: Trinidad and Tobago · General election, 28 April 2025
title: Understanding Trinidad and Tobago's 2025 election
lede: Who won, how a 41-seat Westminster-style vote works, and what the change of government means for the islands and for the Caribbean's fault lines with Venezuela and the United States. Based on the Elections and Boundaries Commission's preliminary results, as of 10 November 2026.

stats.l: seats won by the UNC (21 is a majority)

visual_note: Seats are the Elections and Boundaries Commission's preliminary figures. Early media tallies briefly showed 25 and 14; the Commission's count is 26, 13 and 2.

cells: Centre, led by Kamla Persad-Bissessar; contested with the Coalition of Interests
Governing party since 2015; led into the vote by PM Stuart Young
Tobago autonomy party; won both Tobago seats

table.note: Reported votes: about 334,900 for the UNC, 220,200 for the PNM and 13,900 for the TPP, out of roughly 617,700 cast.

elects: All 41 members of the House of Representatives, for up to five years. Trinidad has 39 seats and Tobago has two. The prime minister is whoever can command a majority in the House, and the President appoints that person.
The 31-member Senate is not elected. The President appoints it on the advice of the government (16), the opposition (6) and independents (9), so the House result sets the balance there too.

system.oneline: First past the post, constituency by constituency: the candidate with the most votes wins the seat, and the party that wins 21 seats governs.

steps.p: Each voter picks one candidate in their constituency. There is no second vote and no party list.
A candidate needs only more votes than anyone else, not a majority. The map's colours show each winner and the size of the margin.

The UNC won about 54% of votes cast and 63% of seats. Nine seats changed hands, seven to the UNC and two to the TPP. In this system a swing of a few points in marginal constituencies can move the whole result.
Tobago also has its own House of Assembly with separate elections. This vote was for the national House only, and the TPP took both Tobago seats from the PNM.

home: The result ended ten years of PNM government and returned Kamla Persad-Bissessar to the job she held from 2010 to 2015. She framed the win around pensions, hospitals and the state's finances, and has named crime reduction and energy security as her top priorities.

home.p: Coverage framed the vote around economic and security worries. The UNC also took two PNM strongholds in south-west Trinidad. After the loss, Stuart Young resigned as party chairman and Keith Rowley said he would step down as leader.

home.h: A narrow base for a wide win
home.p: Turnout of about 54% was the lowest on record. The UNC's majority is real, but it was built on a large share of a smaller electorate, and the PNM is already positioning for a comeback.

world.p: The new government sits much closer to the Trump administration than the PNM did on security and migration, and welcomed a US warship visit. The prime minister has publicly backed US strikes on suspected drug boats off Venezuela, which has drawn criticism at home and in the region.

world.h: Venezuela and the Dragon gas field
world.p: Trinidad's gas economy has long relied on cross-border projects. Washington revoked the licence for the Dragon field in April 2025 and granted a six-month licence in October 2025. By April 2026 the government had recognised Delcy Rodríguez and said it would send a delegation to Caracas to secure its share of jointly owned oil and gas.

Persad-Bissessar said CARICOM was no longer a reliable partner and that Trinidad would seek “new frontiers”, then said she was not leaving. In June 2026 she signalled the country would not be bound by CARICOM's political or security framework. The PNM argues this risks isolating the country.

p: Had the PNM kept power, the likeliest difference would have been tone rather than direction on Venezuela gas, since the PNM government also secured the Dragon licence in 2023. The PNM now says the current government's posture risks isolating the country within CARICOM.
At home, another PNM term would have meant continuity on crime and economic management. After ten years, voters chose a change.
